body:
@robwoodgate , any thoughts on this? I think you've looked at similar ideas, and maybe already made your own PR on this

I'm saying that blind signing and nut09 signature restore is keyed on B_: **only**; the amount and the keysetid are irrelevant. I would go further and eventually drop the 'id' and 'amount' field from the nut09 request

This might be ambiguous around retries. Should the mint remember the keyset that was active when the melt quote was initially created, or just at the start of the current (retry) attempt?

How about adding something like this:

> If a melt fails, the acceptance of its blank change outputs is revoked. Any subsequent melt attempt using the same quote must be treated as a new request

> This might be ambiguous around retries. Should the mint remember the keyset that was active when the melt quote was initially created, or just at the start of the current (retry) attempt?
> 
> How about adding something like this:
> 
> > If a melt fails, the acceptance of its blank change outputs is revoked. Any subsequent melt attempt using the same quote must be treated as a new request

Thanks! I think the current wording covers it. The check is at the acceptance of blinded outputs (in mint, melt or swap), not the creation of a melt quote. Melt quote creation doesn't involve sending blinded outputs.

After a failed melt, the quote is UNPAID again and the next `POST` request is a new request, checked against the keyset state at that time. 

The only "retry" scenario would be a NUT-19 cached request, and that would replay the cached response.

> @robwoodgate , any thoughts on this? I think you've looked at similar ideas, and maybe already made your own PR on this
> 
> I'm saying that blind signing and nut09 signature restore is keyed on B_: **only**; the amount and the keysetid are irrelevant. I would go further and eventually drop the 'id' and 'amount' field from the nut09 request

Yep, #443 already has this in NUT-00: “B_ MUST be unique across the entire mint”, rejecting with 11003/11004. Mint-wide covers any amount or keyset.

I think the `B_` space is large enough we can keep it unique per mint, and with that being the case, agree the NUT-09 lookup COULD request based on just the B_'s, and not the full `BlindedMessage`.
